title: Software Engineer (gn) @ Stealth AI Venture, Berlin
description: What we're building Factories run on machines that generate huge amounts of data, and almost none of it gets used. We're changing that. Our two founders both held C-level roles at leading German robotics ventures. They have spent years bringing advanced technology onto real shop floors, and now they're hiring the founding team. The role You'll build the software that makes sense of what happens on a manufacturing floor. That includes sensor measurements, actuator states, quality measurements, and operational events, streamed from connected machines and autonomous systems. Our platform processes this data to power analysis and automated workflows. We work AI-first. Our coding agents know our platform and our engineering practices, and you'll use them every day. You're still the engineer, though. You'll review every line, understand what it does, and test it properly. That frees you to focus on the application, the industrial domain, and the quality of the system. We care about what you can show, how fast you learn, and whether you take ownership. Seniority and years of experience matter less. What you'll do Own features end to end: understand the problem, choose the approach, then build, test, ship, and follow up Get to know the existing codebase in depth, including its architecture, dependencies, data flows, and failure modes Write code with AI tools and review each change line by line for correctness, maintainability, security, and impact on the wider system Build meaningful unit, integration, and end-to-end tests and wire them into CI Test against messy real-world data, using recorded streams, representative datasets, and simulated devices. Cover missing or delayed measurements, duplicate or out-of-order events, invalid values, and dropped connections Reproduce failures, fix them, and add regression tests so they don't return. Make sure tests reflect the intended behavior, and challenge the assumptions in the implementation Build and improve backend services, APIs, and data pipelines for industrial analytics, knowledge retrieval, and automated workflows Learn how our users and their factories work, so you can spot the right improvements and make good engineering calls Help wherever it's needed: integration, deployment, documentation, and technical investigation. We care about evidence that you can engineer, not about a title or a specific path. Bonus points Depth in one of these areas makes you a particularly strong candidate. We don't expect all three. ML and industrial data: strong ML fundamentals and hands-on work with time-series, sensor, machine, or robotics data. You've dealt with data quality, evaluated models, and turned results into useful product behavior Agents, autonomous systems, and industrial automation: agent coordination, workflow orchestration, state management, or failure handling. IIoT experience, such as telemetry pipelines, device interfaces, MQTT, or OPC UA, is a big plus Knowledge graphs and retrieval: knowledge representation, graph database design, schema and relationship modeling, graph queries, or retrieval that connects structured knowledge to what the application needs Also useful: cloud deployment, containers, and testing software against simulators or physical devices. title: Lead .NET Engineer
description: Location : Onsite, full time at our Buyerlink office right on the Inner Harbour of Victoria, BC! Working hours: Standard full-time business hours, with an early overlap window with our Armenia team About the role We operate a marketplace that connects car shoppers with dealers and manufacturers. The systems behind it run on .NET, they are customer facing, and they carry live transaction volume every hour of the day. When something goes wrong, dealers notice, consumers notice, and revenue moves. That is the level of consequence this role sits at. This is the platform ownership role. You will set the technical direction for the marketplace platform, make the architecture calls, and be the person accountable for its health. Two engineers cover it, you in North America and a senior engineer in Armenia. That is a deliberate design: an eleven hour offset means the marketplace has senior engineering attention through the working day on both sides of the world, which matters for a system our customers use around the clock. What gets built, in what order, and what moves overnight is yours to decide. This is not a role where you take tickets off a queue. You will be one of a small number of people who understand these systems deeply, and you will be expected to act like it. How the role is structured You will report to our VP of Engineering and work daily with engineering, product, and business colleagues across the United States, Latin America, Armenia, and Ukraine. Our US stakeholders will come to you directly, and translating what they need into technical work is a real part of the job. You will lead the senior .NET engineer in Armenia on this platform. You set their technical direction, decide what they pick up, and review what comes back. To be precise about the boundary, this is technical leadership rather than people management. Their employment relationship sits with our Armenia organization, so hiring, performance, and compensation are not yours. Everything about how the platform gets built is. The practical shape of it is a handoff twice a day. What you leave behind at the end of yours determines how their day goes, and the reverse. Leads who write things down and give context in advance get real leverage out of the offset. Leads who keep the important context in their heads do not. One thing to be clear about: as the platform owner in this hemisphere, production issues that surface outside the Armenia working day come to you. What you will do Own the design, development, testing, and release of features across customer-facing .NET applications and the services behind them. Take production issues from first report to resolved root cause, including the ones that surface during your hours and need a decision now rather than after a meeting. Modernize as you go. Parts of this platform predate current .NET, and moving them forward without interrupting a live marketplace is a core part of the job rather than a side project. Design and build APIs that partners, dealers, and internal systems depend on. Work on SQL Server performance and data design, including query and schema work on systems under real load. Direct the work of the senior engineer in Armenia: set priorities, scope what they take on overnight, review what comes back, and give them enough context to make good calls without you. Build a handoff practice that actually works, so overnight coverage produces progress rather than a queue of questions. Review code and raise the standard of what ships. Translate business requirements from product and marketing partners into technical designs, and push back when the requirement and the system are pointing in different directions. Working with AI Every developer here has Claude and GitHub Copilot, and they are part of how the work gets done rather than an optional extra. What matters to us is judgment: knowing which tasks to hand to a model and which to write yourself, giving it enough context to return something usable, and reviewing what comes back as carefully as you would review any other engineer's pull request. You should be able to explain every line you merge. The more important thing to know is where this is heading. Over the next six to twelve months we expect to move substantially toward agentic development, with agents taking on larger and more autonomous portions of the build and test cycle. That will change our tooling, our workflow, and what the day-to-day job looks like. We are not asking you to have done this before, because very few people have. We are asking you to be genuinely interested in figuring it out with us, and comfortable working in an environment where the way we build is still being reshaped. If you would rather join a team with a settled toolchain, this is an honest reason to look elsewhere. If that prospect is the interesting part, we should talk. What you bring 5 to 8 years building and supporting production .NET applications, including time as the senior person others came to. Strong C# and ASP.NET, across both modern .NET and the older framework versions that real businesses still run on. API design and development experience, including integrations that external partners depend on. Real SQL Server depth: query optimization, indexing, and schema design against systems under load. Production experience on Azure. Our platform runs there. Enough front-end familiarity (JavaScript, HTML, CSS) to work effectively on customer-facing applications. Judgment about legacy code. Knowing when to modernize, when to leave it alone, and how to tell the difference. Experience directing other engineers' work, formally or not. You should be able to describe a time you set someone else's technical direction and what you did when it went sideways. Comfort working through change. Our stack and our development practices are actively evolving, and you should find that energizing rather than unsettling. Clear written communication. A distributed team with overnight handoffs runs on writing. Nice to have Experience in automotive, marketplaces, lead generation, or another high-volume transactional domain. Migration experience, particularly legacy .NET Framework to modern .NET, or on-premises SQL Server to Azure SQL. Multi-threading and parallel processing work. Familiarity with XML and XSLT, which appear in parts of this platform. CI/CD and automated testing practice. Agile delivery in a distributed team. Why work with us The systems here matter and the team is small enough that you will see the effect of your work directly. We invest ahead of the curve on tooling, we retire what no longer serves us, and we would rather ship and learn than deliberate indefinitely. If you want scope rather than a slice of someone else's plan, there is plenty of it. Compensation Salary Range: $110, 000 - $130, 000 CAD Compensation will be determined by factors including knowledge and skills, role-specific qualifications, market location, and experience.

title: Senior Fullstack Software Developer (.NET Core/C#)
description: Senior Fullstack Software Developer (.NET Core/C#) Location: Laval, Quebec – Hybrid (Yes, our job postings are intentionally longer than others. Though they will provide you with a realistic job preview and guidance on how best to present your application. We suggest reading in full.) About SOVRA SOVRA is a leading public procurement platform trusted by more than 7,000 government agencies and over 1 million suppliers across North America. Our work sits at the intersection of technology, public service, and accountability, helping governments operate more efficiently and transparently on behalf of the communities they serve. What makes SOVRA unique is our deep focus on the public sector. Our solutions are purpose-built to solve real, complex procurement challenges, balancing compliance with usability and innovation. That commitment has been recognized with the Achievement of Excellence in Procurement (AEP) Certification from the National Procurement Institute, reflecting our high standards and impact on the market. At SOVRA, the work you do matters. Every improvement we make helps public organizations stretch taxpayer dollars further, operate with greater transparency, and deliver better outcomes for millions of people. We're a growing, mission-driven company where smart, curious people come together to build technology that serves the public good. Learn more at sovra.com . Job Setting SOVRA is adding a Senior Fullstack Software Developer to its engineering team to support the growth of a complex, rules-driven web application. This is a new headcount addition, created to meet the demands of an expanding product that requires both depth of engineering judgment and a working understanding of how AI-assisted development fits into a mature delivery process. The role sits within an eleven-person team responsible for a legal document authoring platform built on .NET Core in C# with a TypeScript front end. The application manages layered business rules across multiple document templates, and the person in this role contributes across the full stack, from API design and backend logic to front-end implementation and quality assurance collaboration. The work requires a developer who can read AI-generated code critically and take ownership of whether it is correct and appropriate to the problem at hand. Current documentation is in French, and the team operates in French and English; full English and French bilingual proficiency is essential. What will your main responsibilities look like? Backend Development & Architecture You design, develop, and maintain web application features, microservices, and APIs using .NET Core in C#, with consistent attention to performance, security, and scalability. You participate in technical analysis, solution design, and deployment, and you contribute to corrective maintenance and the ongoing evolution of the application. You apply the organization’s security standards—including OWASP and CWE/SANS25 practices—and verify that implemented features meet those standards before release. Frontend Development You develop front-end features in TypeScript, working within a codebase where the team is actively migrating front-end components to Angular and React. You navigate a complex set of business rules and logic trees that govern how legal documents are assembled, ensuring that new features integrate cleanly with existing template structures. AI-Assisted Development You work within a development process where code is generated by AI tooling, applying your engineering judgment to assess whether the output is correct, complete, and appropriate to the problem being solved. You use AI to generate unit tests that validate the quality and reliability of developed features, and you collaborate with the QA team to develop test scenarios and support test automation. Team Collaboration & Standards You work closely with the product team, development team, and QA to propose technical solutions that meet business needs and hold up under the complexity the application carries. You document your code in French to support long-term maintenance, knowledge transfer, and the team’s shared understanding of the codebase. You monitor developments in engineering practices and tooling, and you actively share what you find with the team. What will you bring to this role? Fullstack development track record — you have software development in a comparable environment, with proven delivery across backend and frontend layers, typically 8+ years of experience .NET Core and C# proficiency — you have strong, hands-on experience building and maintaining APIs and web applications in .NET Core using C#, and you can reason clearly about performance, scalability, and security decisions in that stack. Frontend development experience — you have practical experience developing in TypeScript utilizing Angular or React libraries, and you are comfortable working within a front-end codebase that spans both frameworks. Security and quality standards — you have solid knowledge of OWASP and CWE/SANS25 practices for vulnerability detection and protection, and you apply them as a routine part of development rather than as an afterthought. SQL database experience — you have worked with SQL databases in a production environment and understand how data modelling choices affect application behavior. AI-assisted development fluency — you have experience working with AI development agents, and you bring the engineering maturity to evaluate AI-generated code critically Full French–English bilingualism — you are fully proficient in French and English, both spoken and written Authorization to work in Canada — we are not able to sponsor work visas or transfers at this time. Formal education in software development — you hold a college diploma or bachelor’s degree in software development, computer science, or a related field. Candidates with equivalent professional experience are equally encouraged to apply. What we look for in applications We review every application individually and assess it on its own merits rather than screening for keywords. The most remarkable applications are specific: They provide details of your work and read more like a portfolio than a summary of responsibilities. Describe what you built or delivered, the problem it solved, and the outcome, with numbers wherever you have them. A technology list alone tells us very little. We want to see what languages, frameworks, or tools you used on your deliverables, where, and in what context. Our interview process Our process is designed to be thorough while respecting your time. Three conversations cover your background, the technical substance of the role, and how you would work with the team. Screening with Talent Acquisition — your background, the role, and mutual fit. Technical Interview — your hands-on experience with the stack, your approach to AI-assisted development, and how you reason through engineering problems. Team Interview — how you would work day to day with the development team, QA, and product. Why you should join us SOVRA serves the public sector, and the work carries the weight that comes with that purpose. Every improvement to our platform helps government agencies operate more efficiently and deliver greater value to the communities they serve. We are a company in a period of deliberate growth, and we are looking for professionals who want genuine ownership of their work and a direct hand in building the organization around them. In this role, that ownership is real: your work on SOVRA’s document authoring platform shapes how the team delivers accurate, reliable software to the public sector organizations that depend on it. Our benefits include the following, with full details shared during the hiring process: Comprehensive health and medical coverage. Paid time off. A structured learning and development program. Paid parental leave. If this role aligns with your experience and ambitions, we encourage you to apply. Thank you for your interest in SOVRA. However, only selected candidates will be contacted. At SOVRA, we are committed to fostering an inclusive and equitable workplace. We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate against any employee or applicant for employment based on race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, marital status, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws. We provide a work environment free from discrimination and harassment. In addition, we are committed to ensuring pay equity across our organization and regularly review our compensation practices.
